newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's MTRC sees no large financing until 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: HK's MTRC sees no large financing until 2nd half.

text.p: Hong Kong's Mass Transit Railway Corp (MTRC) does not plan to seek large-scale financing in the first half of 1997, although smaller fundraisings are possible, finance director Clement Kwok said on Monday.
"I do not expect to be signing another transaction of this size in the first half," Kwok said, referring to a HK$5.0 billion revolving credit facility signed on Monday in Hong Kong.
The MTRC plans to borrow some HK$55 billion to HK$60 billion over the next five years to finance construction of its Tseung Kwan O line and to upgrade existing facilities.
It expects to borrow about HK$10 billion this year via issues launched in Hong Kong and overseas, with the United States and Japan likely targets.

In December, treasurer Jimmy Lau said the MTRC predicted a need of some HK$10 billion per annum if the Hong Kong government approved its plan to extend one of its rail lines to Tseung Kwan O in the New Territories.
Hong Kong's Executive Council gave its go-ahead for the project in mid-December.
The MTRC's five-year revolving credit facility signed on Monday attracted 35 banks. The issue was increased to HK$5.0 billion from HK$3.5 billion after being oversubscribed in syndication.
The facility pays an interest margin of 36.5 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 41.5 basis points to top-tier managers.
Kwok said the MTRC might raise money through smaller-sized fundraisings in the first-half of 1997.

These could include Hong Kong dollar denominated bonds issued through the MTRC's note issuance facility in which the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) acts as arranger, custodian, agent and operator.
"The HKMA is an ongoing programme to issue relatively modest amounts from time to time," said Kwok.
The MTRC launched a HK$500 million five-year bond in August 1996, the third tranche of the note issuance programme.
